title: Dragon Dictation Alternatives for Windows (2026)
summary: The best Dragon dictation alternatives for Windows in 2026, plus where Dragon's lineup, prices, and mobile app stand today.
body_markdown:
Dragon has been the default answer to "dictation software for Windows" for so long that a lot of people searching for it have never tried anything else. In 2026 that habit is worth re-examining. The consumer editions have thinned out, the mobile app stopped selling in July, and Nuance's own product page no longer prints a price. Meanwhile the dictation half of what Dragon does, turning speech into accurate text in any app, has gotten cheaper and better elsewhere. This guide covers where Dragon stands today, what Windows already gives you for free, and the alternatives worth your time.


**The short answer:** for everyday dictation on Windows, Aqua Voice is the best Dragon alternative in 2026: accurate without voice training, a custom dictionary, and text you can edit by voice. Windows 11 ships free voice typing and Voice Access worth trying first. Wispr Flow, Talon Voice, Superwhisper, and open-source Whisper apps cover narrower needs.


## Where Dragon stands in 2026


Before choosing a replacement, it helps to know what you would be replacing, because the Dragon lineup is smaller than most roundups admit. These are the current facts from Nuance's own pages and store listings at the time of writing.


- **Dragon Professional v16 is the product.** Nuance describes it as "optimized for Windows 11 and backwards-compatible to Windows 10." It is a perpetual desktop license (no subscription) and the version has not changed since 2023. Nuance's product page no longer shows a price; the only button is "Contact us." Authorized resellers list the individual edition in the $699 range, so treat that as the going rate rather than an official figure.
- **Dragon Professional Anywhere and Dragon Legal Anywhere** are the cloud-hosted, subscription versions, sold by quote through Nuance and its partners. If you are considering either, ask for the support timeline in writing before you commit.
- **Dragon Anywhere Mobile is no longer sold.** The app's own release notes in the App Store state: "As of July 1, 2026, Dragon Anywhere Mobile is no longer available for sale. Purchasing new subscriptions and renewing existing subscriptions is no longer possible." Existing subscribers keep access until their term ends. If you dictated on your phone and synced to Dragon on your PC, that half of the workflow is going away.
- **Dragon Home is gone from the lineup.** The consumer edition no longer appears among Nuance's products; only the version 15 install guides remain on the support site.
- **There is no Mac version.** Dragon Professional Individual for Mac was discontinued in 2018 and never returned, which is why we wrote a separate[Dragon alternatives for Mac](https://aquavoice.com/blog/dragon-alternatives-for-mac) guide. Dragon today means Windows.
- **Dragon Medical One** continues as Nuance's enterprise healthcare line, sold to clinics and health systems rather than individuals. Clinicians comparing it with newer tools should start with our[medical dictation roundup](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-medical-dictation-software) .


Nothing here says Dragon stopped working. Version 16 runs fine on Windows 11, and for the people who need its deepest features it remains a serious tool. It does mean that a new buyer in 2026 is paying a few hundred dollars up front for software that is three years old, with a shrinking set of companion products around it.


## The two jobs Dragon did


Every honest Dragon alternative list has to start with the same split, because Dragon did two different jobs and most replacements only do one.


1. **Dictation.** Speech in, accurate text out, into whatever app has your cursor, with a vocabulary that spells your names, clients, and jargon correctly. This is what most Dragon owners used every day.
2. **Hands-free control.** Opening apps, clicking, selecting, correcting, and formatting entirely by voice. This is why Dragon mattered to people with RSI, limited mobility, or other accessibility needs, and it is the part newer dictation apps mostly do not attempt.


If you miss the first job, a modern dictation app will beat Dragon on accuracy and price. If you depend on the second, look at Voice Access and Talon below before anything else. The picks are organized around that split.


## Start with what Windows already includes


Windows 11 ships two free voice features, and they are not the same thing. Our[guide to voice to text on Windows 11](https://aquavoice.com/blog/voice-to-text-windows) walks through both in detail; here is the short version for someone coming from Dragon.


- **Voice typing (Win + H).** Press the Windows key and H in any text field, speak, and Windows types. It works on Windows 10 and 11 and handles everyday email and messages well. According to Microsoft's documentation it needs an internet connection, because recognition runs on Microsoft's speech service. There is no custom vocabulary and no way to edit by voice, which is exactly where Dragon users will feel the gap.
- **Voice Access.** This is the accessibility tool, and the closest built-in match for Dragon's control half. It uses on-device recognition, works offline once set up, and lets you open apps, click, scroll, and move the mouse by voice. It requires Windows 11 version 22H2 or later. Microsoft says it replaced the older Windows Speech Recognition on those versions in September 2024.


Try voice typing for a day before you buy anything. If it is accurate enough for what you write, you may be done. Most people who go looking for a Dragon replacement do so because a free tool kept mangling the words that matter to them, and that is where a dedicated model earns its keep.


## The best Dragon alternatives for Windows


### 1. Aqua Voice: best for accurate everyday dictation


We build Aqua Voice, so read this section as informed rather than neutral, and check the verifiable claims yourself.


[Aqua Voice](https://aquavoice.com/) runs natively on[Windows 10 and 11](https://aquavoice.com/windows) and types into any app: Word, Outlook, Chrome, Slack, a CRM field, the terminal. It is powered by[Avalon](https://aquavoice.com/avalon-api) , Aqua's own speech model, which ranked as the top proprietary model on the OpenASR leaderboard at its October 2025 debut (it now sits sixth overall as newer open models have landed). On Aqua's own AISpeak benchmark it reports 97.3% accuracy, a self-reported figure, so weigh it as one data point. For an independent read, 9to5Mac ran the same passage through Apple's built-in dictation and Aqua and counted 17 errors against 1.


Three things matter for Dragon users specifically. There is **no voice training** : Avalon is accurate from the first sentence, with no enrollment reading and no profile to maintain. There is a **custom dictionary** , which is the feature people actually trained Dragon for: add your names, products, and terms once and they come out spelled right. And there is **Edit by voice** : say the change you want ("change meeting to deadline", "delete the last sentence") and Aqua rewrites the text instead of making you reach for the keyboard, which recovers some of the hands-free feel. Final text lands in about 450ms, and you can dictate up to 230 words per minute.


- **Platforms:** Windows, Mac, iPhone, and Android, on one subscription.
- **Languages:** 49.
- **Price:** free for 1,000 words as a lifetime allowance (not a timed trial, no card required), then Pro at $10/mo billed annually, or $12 month to month. See[pricing](https://aquavoice.com/pricing) .
- **Security:** Aqua has a SOC 2 Type II audit report and is ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR and HIPAA compliant, which matters if IT manages your PC.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Aqua is a dictation tool, not a full hands-free control system, and it transcribes in the cloud, so it needs an internet connection. If you need to run your whole PC by voice, or you require fully local processing, keep reading. For the direct comparison, see[Aqua Voice vs Dragon](https://aquavoice.com/vs/dragon) .


### 2. Wispr Flow: the polished cross-platform pick


Wispr Flow is the best-known name in this category and it has a real Windows app alongside Mac, iOS, and Android. It is fast, clean, and pleasant to use, and it tidies your speech as you go.


- **Price at the time of writing:** Pro at $12/mo billed annually or $15 month to month, with a capped free tier.
- **The honest tradeoff:** it processes speech in the cloud, it is one of the pricier options here, and like every dictation app on this list it does not replace Dragon's control half. Wispr says it runs Canto, a speech model it built in-house. We keep an[Aqua Voice vs Wispr Flow](https://aquavoice.com/vs/wispr-flow) comparison up to date.


### 3. Talon Voice: best for serious hands-free control


If the reason you used Dragon was to run the computer without a keyboard or mouse, whether for RSI, limited mobility, or coding by voice, Talon Voice is what the accessibility community actually reaches for. It runs on-device, separates a command mode from a dictation mode, and people drive entire development workflows through it.


- **Platforms:** Windows, Mac, Linux.
- **Price:** a free public version, with the newest builds behind a low-cost Patreon.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Talon is a control framework, not a consumer app. Expect a learning curve and some configuration. The payoff is a ceiling for hands-free control that nothing else on this list reaches, which is why it earns the spot. If Talon itself feels like too much, our[Talon alternatives](https://aquavoice.com/blog/talon-voice-alternatives) guide splits the control job from the dictation job in more detail.


### 4. Superwhisper: best fully offline option


If part of what you liked about Dragon was that it ran on your own machine, Superwhisper is the closest match in spirit. It runs local speech models (including open Whisper builds it lets you choose), so nothing has to leave the PC.


- **Price at the time of writing:** a free tier on the local models, Pro at $8.49/mo, or a one-time lifetime license listed at $249.99.
- **The honest tradeoff:** Superwhisper started on the Mac, and its Windows build still trails the Mac version in features and polish, which the vendor's own release notes make easy to check. Local accuracy also depends on the model you load and the hardware you run it on. See our[Superwhisper alternatives](https://aquavoice.com/blog/superwhisper-alternative) guide for the wider offline field.


### 5. Open-source Whisper apps: free and fully local


If you are comfortable with a little setup, a wave of free, open-source Windows dictation tools wrap OpenAI's Whisper (which they disclose openly) and run entirely on your PC. Projects like OpenWhispr offer push-to-talk dictation with no cloud, no subscription, and no telemetry. You trade polish and a custom dictionary for total control and a $0 price.


### 6. Staying inside Dragon


For a narrow group, no alternative is a drop-in replacement: lawyers and clinicians who depend on Dragon's specialty vocabularies, people with years of custom voice macros, and anyone whose organization has standardized on Dragon Medical One. If that is you, the honest path is Dragon Professional v16 on a perpetual license, or one of the Anywhere subscriptions through a reseller who will put the support dates in writing. Just go in knowing what you are buying: a mature, Windows-only, on-device tool at a one-time price in the $699 range, with no mobile companion going forward.

## How to switch from Dragon without losing your vocabulary


The main thing Dragon owners worry about is the custom vocabulary they spent years building. Here is the practical path.


1. **Export your custom words.** Dragon can export your added words to a text file: in Dragon 15 the path is Tools, Vocabulary Center, Export custom word and phrase list (the label varies by version). Do this before you uninstall anything, even if you are not sure which tool you will land on.
2. **Install the new tool and add the words that matter.** In Aqua, the custom dictionary lives in the app's settings; you do not need to re-add every word, only the names and terms a general model would guess wrong. Most people find the list is much shorter than their Dragon vocabulary, because the model already knows common technical terms.
3. **Learn the one new habit.** Dragon users are used to saying "scratch that" and formatting commands. In Aqua you say what you want changed in plain language, and the[setup guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) covers the commands and shortcuts.
4. **Run both for a week.** Keep Dragon installed while you test. A perpetual license does not expire, so there is no rush to remove it.


## Setting up Aqua Voice on Windows


1. Go to[aquavoice.com/windows](https://aquavoice.com/windows) and download the Windows app (Windows 10 or 11).
2. Sign in. Your account starts with 1,000 free words, no card required.
3. Grant microphone access when Windows prompts you.
4. Set your push-to-talk key, then hold it, speak, and release. The text appears wherever your cursor is, in any app.
5. To fix something, hold the key and say the correction. Edit by voice rewrites the text instead of making you retype.


Because it works system-wide, the same loop covers Word, Outlook, Chrome, Slack, and any form field, and the same account carries to your other devices. If you want to see the whole Windows field before deciding, our[best AI dictation apps for Windows](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-ai-dictation-app-for-windows) roundup goes deeper on each pick.


## How to choose in one minute


- **You mostly want accurate dictation with your own vocabulary:** Aqua Voice.
- **You want the smoothest cloud dictation and price is secondary:** Wispr Flow.
- **You need to run your PC hands-free and want it free:** Windows Voice Access.
- **You need serious hands-free control for accessibility or coding:** Talon Voice.
- **Your hard requirement is that audio never leaves your PC:** Superwhisper or an open-source Whisper app.
- **You depend on specialty vocabularies or years of voice macros:** stay on Dragon Professional v16.


Dragon set the bar for desktop dictation, and nothing on this list rebuilds all of it. But the half most people used, accurate text in every app, is better in 2026 than it ever was on Dragon: no training session, a fraction of the price, and the same account on your phone.[Try Aqua free](https://aquavoice.com/download) on your next email before you decide.


## FAQ


**Is Dragon NaturallySpeaking still available in 2026?**


Yes, as Dragon Professional v16 for Windows, a perpetual desktop license that Nuance describes as optimized for Windows 11 and backwards-compatible to Windows 10. Nuance's product page no longer shows a price and directs buyers to sales; resellers list it in the $699 range. There is no Mac version, and the consumer Dragon Home edition is no longer in the lineup.


**What happened to Dragon Anywhere?**


According to the app's own release notes, Dragon Anywhere Mobile stopped being sold on July 1, 2026, and new subscriptions and renewals are no longer possible. Existing subscribers keep access until their current term ends. Aqua Voice runs on iPhone and Android as well as Windows, on one subscription, if you want a mobile and desktop pair.


**What is the best Dragon alternative for Windows?**


For everyday dictation, Aqua Voice: no voice training, a custom dictionary for your names and terms, Edit by voice, and $10/mo billed annually after 1,000 free words. For hands-free PC control, Windows Voice Access (free, built in) or Talon Voice. For fully offline dictation, Superwhisper or an open-source Whisper app.


**Is there a free Dragon alternative for Windows?**


Yes. Windows 11 includes voice typing (Win + H) and Voice Access at no cost, Talon Voice has a free public version, open-source Whisper apps run locally for free, and Aqua Voice gives you 1,000 words free as a lifetime allowance before its paid plan.
